text: Senné was Szenna (Ungszenna) in Ung county. Its Roman Catholic register of births, marriages and deaths, 1831-1926, was microfilmed; the originals are in the Prešov state archive. Per the Places agent (note of 12 Nov 2026): films 1793682 and 1793683; in this title baptisms run 1866 to 1912, marriages 1863 to 1926, deaths 1831 to 1925, and earlier baptisms are in older volumes not yet traced.
Iňačovce was Solymos in Ung county. Listed registers: Greek Catholic 1811-1898, Reformed 1747-1940, Roman Catholic 1863-1926.
FamilySearch catalogues Greek Catholic records of the Mukachevo Eparchy for Ungvár / Užhorod and the Ung district, 1826-1938. Candidate home for the Maria Demko entry.
A FamilySearch community thread reports that none of the surviving 1869 census sheets in the Slovakia collection are from Ung county. This conflicts with PR-3 and needs the original image to settle.
Montreal Gazette, 13 Feb 1928, p. 12: a John Duska burned by molten copper at Port Colborne, Ontario. No connection shown. Worth checking against H-002 and H-003.

The Iňačovce municipal website names Dúška among the families living in the village in the 18th century, and says the village was resettled after 1720 from northern Ung and Zemplén. A village website with no archive reference; the source list behind it has not been seen.

Viszoka had no Greek Catholic parish of its own in the 19th century. Its Greek Catholics belonged to the Čičarovce (Csicser) Greek Catholic parish from about 1806. Čičarovce was the seat of three parishes at once: Roman Catholic, Greek Catholic and Reformed.
Greek Catholic registers of Čičarovce are reported kept from 1789 and held complete at the State Archive in Prešov. Greek Catholic registers of Iňačovce, which served Senné, run from 1811.

Csurgovich is a Greek Catholic clerical family of the Mukachevo eparchy: a canon Joannes Csurgovich and a teacher Andreas Csurgovich appear in the 1843 schematism. Where the priest of 1882 served was not established.
A Slovak Academy of Sciences booklet lists Hreško and Hricko as separate surnames, both formed from Gregor.
Belža is a Greek Catholic parish whose filials today include Gyňov and Seňa. No 1890s directory was seen to confirm the same for 1894 to 1895.

The Senné municipal history: a Roman Catholic parish under Szatmár from 1804 with Stretavka and Iňačovce among its filials; oldest surviving registers from 1778; in 1904 the village counted 484 Roman Catholics and 231 Greek Catholics. It names no Duska or Demko.
The 1869 census for Ung county is reported held in the Uzhhorod archives and was not filmed by FamilySearch.
The Kulin family held land at Kisszeretva (Stretavka) in the urbarial tables of the 1770s; their noble predicate was bánhegyesi, so "de K. Sz." in 1838 is more likely a residence than a title.
A regional association's page on Senné says many emigrated between 1870 and 1890.
The Dictionary of American Family Names derives Demko from a pet form of Demeter or Demyan. The name arose in many villages independently and says nothing about rite or ethnicity.

Places agent, from the Prešov state archive's catalogue of church registers (PL-R-003, PL-S-075, note PL-N-026 @208af51): the Iňačovce Greek Catholic register is four volumes on film 88: no. 380 (1811 to 1831, Latin), no. 381 (1831 to 1859, Church Slavonic, Latin, Hungarian), no. 382 (births 1861 to 1870, Latin) and no. 383 (births 1870 to 1898). Births of 1860 are in no listed volume. Its district is Iňačovce, Jastrabie, Senné and Stretava. Which volume and page each of the 58 strips of folder F-005 comes from is not established.

Places agent (same catalogue, @208af51): Senné Roman Catholic births exist at Prešov only from 1866, in volume no. 1089; deaths are in no. 1091 (1831 to 1886) and no. 1093 (1887 to 1925). The baptism of Michal Duska, if he was born at Senné between 1895 and 1908, should be in no. 1089; burials that would test a reused name are in no. 1093.

Places agent (PL-R-005 @208af51): the Reformed of Iňačovce have a register of their own within the Lúčky parish, no. 592/1: births 1819 to 1927, marriages 1820 to 1926, deaths 1819 to 1936. This is where Anna Duska, Reformed, mother at Solymos 43 in 1894, should be sought.

The Hungaricana archive portal has urbarial tables by village. Its pages for Solymos and Szenna in Ung county give landlords and head counts that match the owner's images exactly, so the images are very probably from there. The pages show no date and no archive reference; the larger images may be there.

Valentine Democrat (Valentine, Nebraska), 19 January 1911, page 2, in the Nebraska Newspapers archive: the Niobrara hotel explosion at 7.30 on Sunday evening, 15 January. The owner, Michael Kendall, went to the cellar after a gas leak and is thought to have struck a match. Dead: Kendall, his son Kenneth, 'Ann Duseka, a cook', and Roy Crosby, a travelling salesman. Read through a text extract of the page, not from the image.

From the owner's translated guide (made 23 May 2022 from a page of the Hungaricana library portal): the Czechoslovak census of 1921 for Subcarpathian Rus' survives almost whole, about 270,000 pages, in the Berehove (Beregszász) section of the Transcarpathian Regional State Archives, and was conserved and digitised in 2017. It has summary sheets by settlement and house, and household forms, bilingual Czech and Hungarian, with date and place of birth, mother tongue, religion and occupation. Whether Senné and Iňačovce, which lay west of the Uh, are in that collection is not said and is for the Places agent.

Places agent, holdings entry PL-R-001 @641ba53 (status confirmed): the Senné Roman Catholic register at the Prešov state archive is church registers catalogue nos. 1089 to 1093, microfilm 287-288: births 1866 to 1912 (1089), marriages 1863 to 1886 and 1887 to 1926 (1090, 1092), deaths 1831 to 1886 and 1887 to 1925 (1091, 1093); filmed as FamilySearch catalogue 710997, films 1793682 and 1793683. Used here as the archive reference for the marriage of 1892 and the baptism strips of folder F-009.

Four of the owner's word files are lists of links to the Slovakiana portal (slovakiana.sk), one link for each household sheet of the census of 1930: Senné in the Veľké Kapušany district (two versions of the list, 143 and 151 different sheets), Iňačovce (168) and Seňa by Košice (8). They hold a title line and links, nothing else. Use: every household of Senné in 1930 can be read one by one, which would find every Duska house there and the sheets for the houses of György Duska's descendants. Not yet done. The owner, asked whether to do this now: no, at the end (S-000-14).

The owner's note of a portal search dated '4/3/2022': the census of 1930 returned 10,728 results for the Michalovce district and 4,356 for Veľké Kapušany. A measure of the collection's size, nothing more.

Places agent, PL-N-041 @fc7360d, from the Prešov archive's catalogue: all four volumes of the Iňačovce Greek Catholic register hold burials. No. 380: deaths 1811 to 1826 at pp. 138 to 165 and 1827 to 1831 at pp. 167 to 190. No. 381: 1831 to 1859 at pp. 154 to 255. No. 382, counted in leaves: 1861 to 1874 at leaves 83 to 141 (leaf 106 is December 1864). No. 383: from 1860, at pp. 215 to 295. All on microfilm 88. The catalogue breaks no. 380 at 1826, where the form of the strips changes.

Demko agent, research note DM-B-020 @6623439, on the owner's Y branch R-FTB41229. By that note: the branch sits in haplogroup R1a under Z280 > Z92 > Y4459 > YP5520; a public tree lists two samples on it, one from Kujawsko-Pomorskie in Poland and one with no country; the wider branch Y4459 has 2,226 tested descendants, most of those with a country in Russia (302), Ukraine (120) and Poland (80); Z92 is described as commonest among Balts and East Slavs and low among Poles, Slovaks and Hungarians (a secondary summary the Demko agent marks unchecked). Of the owner's matches the note gives counts only: seventeen men, all at the twelve-marker level; the five tested in full differ from him at 25 to 43 markers; none is on his branch; none is a Duska. Its conclusion: the result 'leans, weakly, toward an eastern origin', cannot tell Rusyn from Slovak, and no male-line relative within the time of records has tested. Taken here as a lead: none of the tree figures is checked by this agent, which has run no search on the branch name (DEC below).

Tiba is the Hungarian name of Tibava, a village in the present district of Sobrance, in the old county of Ung, twenty to thirty kilometres north-east of Senné; it had a Greek Catholic church (all recalled from training, not sourced). If so, Anna Krak's baptism and her marriage to György Duska belong in the Greek Catholic books that served Tibava. Put to the Places agent at B-057: which parish, which volumes at Prešov, and whether Krak is a Tibava surname.

The Montreal Gazette's obituary page for Michael Duska, published 22 June 2019, as given by the owner. This agent's fetch of the page was refused by the site, so the text in D-015-15 is the owner's paste and has not been compared with the page.
